newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stocks take breather but seen solid.
newsitem.headline: German stocks take breather but seen solid.

text.p: German shares edged further down in afternoon trade on Wednesday after closing the bourse session marginally lower, but dealers said the current high price levels appeared secure, albeit on thin trading volumes.
The 30-share IBIS DAX was down 3.77 points at 2,622.66 at 1302 GMT, just below their bourse close at 2,625.70.

But a report showing an unexpectedly weak U.S. trade balance was helping support Bunds and -- indirectly -- shares in the afternoon and the firm dollar was also a continued positive factor, dealers said.
Dollar-driven car shares were among the best performers.
"We certainly are not seeing any huge selling pressure here, turnover has been moderate. I don't think this indicates a downward trend," said a Munich dealer.
The next major market factor would likely be the expiry Friday of options and futures contracts on the DAX, which often triggers a substantial move on the cash market.
"I think the 2,650 level might be one to watch," one dealer said.
The release of the Ifo business confidence index, which last month showed an unexpectedly sharp rise, should also attract attention at its expected release on Thursday.
Car shares were steady with Daimler-Benz AG up 30 pfennigs at 83.62 marks in later trade and Volkswagen AG, off earlier highs, up 10 pfennigs at 573.10.
Electronics and engineering giant Siemens AG was up 42 pfennigs at 79.22, which dealers attributed to technical factors, possibly related to the options expiry.
